s.note: Poached shrimp, cocktail sauce, iceberg, lemon.
s.how: Bring a pot of salted water to the boil with the bay leaves and half the lemon, add the prawns and poach until just pink, about 2 minutes. Plunge into iced water, then drain and chill. Mix the mayo, tomato sauce, Tabasco and a squeeze of lemon for the Marie Rose. Fill 4 coupes with lettuce and avocado, hang the prawns over the rim and spoon over the sauce. Dust with paprika and serve with lemon wedges.

s.note: Crab beignets, Creole remoulade, lemon. Frank says grace at the Strongs' table.
s.how: Whisk the flour, baking powder, egg and milk to a thick batter, then fold in the crab, spring onion and Cajun seasoning. Mix the mayo, mustard, capers and a squeeze of lemon for the remoulade. Fry spoonfuls in 180C oil, turning, until puffed and golden, about 3 minutes. Drain, salt and serve hot with the remoulade and lemon.

m.n: Filet mignon from the aisle cart
m.note: Filet with béarnaise, pommes dauphine and beans, served from the first class cart.
m.how: Boil and mash the potatoes dry. Heat 60ml water with 30g of the butter, beat in the flour, then the eggs, and mix into the mash. Fry spoonfuls of the potato in 180C oil until puffed and golden for the pommes dauphine. Simmer the vinegar with the shallot and half the tarragon until almost gone, whisk in the yolks over low heat, then the 120g melted butter in a thin stream. Stir in the rest of the tarragon. Sear the seasoned steaks in the oil and remaining butter, about 4 minutes a side for medium-rare, and rest. Blanch the beans and plate everything the way the cart did it, sauce on the side.
shop: 4 beef eye fillet steaks, about 200g each@Meat

w.n: Bucket of cream pots de creme
w.note: Vanilla custard pots with brown butter shortbread. Two little mice fell in a bucket of cream.
w.how: Heat the cream with the vanilla until steaming. Whisk the yolks and caster sugar, then whisk in the hot cream. Strain into 4 small pots in a roasting tin, pour hot water halfway up and bake at 150C until set with a wobble. Beat the browned butter with the icing sugar, mix in the flour and salt, press into a tin and bake at 160C until golden. Chill the pots and serve with a wedge of the shortbread.

d.note: Rye, sweet vermouth, bitters and a cherry, worn with pinstripes.
d.how: Stir the rye, vermouth and bitters with plenty of ice until very cold. Strain into 4 chilled coupes. Add a cherry and twist a strip of orange peel over each.
